allowlist.reason: The README migration section names the old installation and exact Pier runtime contracts that must be preserved during in-place upgrades.
Installation and rollback instructions must retain exact legacy filesystem, account, binary, and systemd identifiers.
This is the explicit compatibility migration guide; old identifiers are operational commands and migration source names, not the current product identity.
One nominative lineage statement identifies the upstream codebase and distinguishes it from the MOONSHIPS product brand.
The security scope explicitly distinguishes retained legacy runtime identifiers from the public product name.
These renamed files preserve upstream legal texts for historical attribution only; the header explicitly states they are not MOONSHIPS policy or agreements.
These archived translated READMEs are inherited upstream documents; their leading notice points readers to current MOONSHIPS documentation.
Cargo workspace member names and source comments are compatibility identifiers and are not public-facing product labels.
Crate and executable package names remain unchanged to preserve existing build and runtime contracts.
CI invokes the legacy-named updater script and the retained pier-core package/binary test target; these are compatibility identifiers.
Release artifact filenames retain legacy executable names consumed by existing installers and nodes.
The comment documents the retained Pier-compatible crate/runtime boundary; the UI color namespace is MOONSHIPS.

Exact legacy service, updater, federation wire-header, cookie, browser-storage, container-name, and protocol identifiers are retained for compatibility; standalone public product labels are rejected by the scanner.
Locale occurrences are retained technical identifiers shown in commands, service names, environment variables, and network labels; descriptive product copy is MOONSHIPS.
Bootstrap must download and install the existing binary names and preserve PIER_* configuration and filesystem/service contracts.
Installer compatibility paths, users, service units, binary names, and PIER_* environment variables are intentionally unchanged.
The updater filename, systemd state, log tags, binary names, and environment variables are existing runtime contracts.
The systemd unit identity and executable path are intentionally retained for existing installations.
The privileged helper unit identity and executable path are intentionally retained for existing installations.

Ecosystem audit, security review, architecture, migration, and historical source documents must name the legacy Pier lineage and MOONSHIPS product when describing source repositories, implementation paths, and compatibility boundaries; these references are intentional technical documentation, not stale repository destinations.
